IRドロップ.desc: The drop in supply voltage reaching a circuit because current (I) flows through the resistance (R) of the power wiring. It increases delay and can cause malfunctions.

クロストーク.desc: Noise that appears on one wire when the signal on a neighboring wire changes, mainly through capacitive coupling. Wider spacing and shield wires reduce it.

パッシベーション膜.desc: A film formed as the topmost layer of a chip to protect the circuitry from moisture, contamination and mechanical damage. Silicon nitride and polyimide are typical materials.

裏面電源供給.desc: Placing the power wiring on the back of the wafer so the front-side wiring can be used for signals. It reduces voltage drop and routing congestion.

MOL(ミドル・オブ・ライン).desc: The contacts and local interconnects that link transistors (FEOL) to the multilevel wiring (BEOL). With scaling, their resistance has grown and now limits performance.

表皮効果.desc: The concentration of high-frequency current near the surface of a conductor, which raises its effective resistance. The higher the frequency, the thinner the surface layer carrying the current.

ブラックの式.desc: An empirical formula for interconnect lifetime under electromigration in terms of current density and temperature. Lifetime is inversely proportional to a power of current density and falls exponentially as temperature rises.

ダイシング.desc: Cutting a wafer into individual chips (dies). Besides sawing with a rotating blade, there are methods such as stealth dicing, which forms a modified layer inside the wafer with a laser.

ダイボンディング.desc: Attaching and fixing a diced chip at its position on a lead frame or package substrate, using adhesive, solder or sintered material.

バックグラインド.desc: Grinding the back of a wafer before dicing to thin it for packaging. Chips for stacking are thinned to a few tens of micrometers.

WLP(ウエハレベルパッケージ).desc: A package in which redistribution wiring and external terminals are formed while the chips are still in wafer form, before dicing. The result is a small package about the size of the chip.

CSP(チップサイズパッケージ).desc: A general term for packages shrunk to nearly the size of the chip. They are widely used in compact devices such as smartphones.

リフローはんだ付け.desc: Printing solder paste on a circuit board, placing components and heating everything in an oven to melt the solder. It is the standard method for surface mounting.

熱抵抗.desc: A measure of how hard it is for heat to flow, in °C/W. Multiplying dissipated power by thermal resistance gives the temperature rise. Junction-to-ambient thermal resistance is written θJA.

ウエハテスト(プローブテスト).desc: Checking the electrical characteristics of each chip on the wafer by touching probes to its pads before dicing. It finds bad chips before assembly so they are not packaged needlessly.

BIST(組み込み自己テスト).desc: Test circuitry built into the chip so that it generates test patterns and checks results by itself. It is widely used, for example, to test memories.

ATPG(自動テストパターン生成).desc: Automatically generating test patterns that detect faults from a circuit's netlist. It is used together with scan design.

縮退故障.desc: The basic fault model in logic testing, which assumes a signal line is stuck at 0 or 1.

故障検出率(フォールトカバレッジ).desc: The fraction of modeled faults that a set of test patterns can detect. The higher it is, the less likely defective chips are to escape.

IDDQテスト.desc: A test that measures the supply current of a CMOS circuit at rest and flags defects such as bridging faults when it is abnormally high.

KGD(ノウングッドダイ).desc: A chip confirmed to be good before packaging. It matters when several chips go into one package, because a single bad chip ruins the whole module.

パレート図.desc: A chart that lists items such as defect types as bars in descending order of count, with a line for the cumulative share. It shows which items to tackle first.

管理図.desc: A chart that plots process measurements over time against a center line and control limits (usually ±3σ) to judge whether the process is stable. Points outside the limits or runs on one side signal problems.

特性要因図.desc: A diagram that organizes the causes affecting a problem (the effect) in the shape of a fish skeleton. Also called a fishbone diagram.

FMEA(故障モード影響解析).desc: A method that lists the possible failure modes of a product or process, evaluates their effects and severity, and plans countermeasures in advance.

APC(先進的プロセス制御).desc: Automatically adjusting the process settings for the next lot or wafer based on earlier measurements, as in run-to-run control. It reduces variation.

システマティック不良.desc: A defect that occurs repeatedly at particular patterns or locations because of interactions between design and process. It is distinguished from random defects caused by chance particles.

アレニウスモデル.desc: A model in which reaction or degradation rates vary with temperature as exp(−Ea/kT). It is used to estimate lifetime at operating temperature from accelerated tests at higher temperatures.

FIT.desc: A unit of failure rate: 1 FIT is one failure per billion (10⁹) device-hours. It is used for parts with very low failure rates, such as semiconductors.

ワイブル分布.desc: A probability distribution widely used to analyze lifetime data. Its shape parameter can represent early-failure, random-failure and wear-out behavior.

ホットキャリア注入(HCI).desc: Degradation in which carriers accelerated by the strong field near the drain are injected into the gate insulator, shifting the threshold voltage and reducing drive current.

ラッチアップ.desc: A condition in which a parasitic thyristor structure in a CMOS circuit turns on and a large current keeps flowing between supply and ground. It is prevented by well-contact placement, guard rings and similar measures.

ESD(静電気放電).desc: A sudden discharge of static electricity from a charged person or object. Applied to an IC pin it can destroy gate oxides and other structures, so I/O pins have protection circuits.

ソフトエラー.desc: A temporary flip of data stored in memory or flip-flops caused by neutrons from cosmic rays, alpha particles and the like. The device is not damaged, so rewriting restores correct operation.

ネットリスト.desc: Data describing the elements (cells) of a circuit and how they are connected. It is the output of logic synthesis and the input to place-and-route and timing analysis.

スタンダードセル.desc: A pre-designed, pre-verified building block such as a logic gate or flip-flop. Cells share a common height so automatic place-and-route can line them up to build large circuits.

PDK(プロセスデザインキット).desc: The set of design data a foundry gives to designers, including design rules, device models, cell libraries and verification rule decks.

テープアウト.desc: Handing over the finished, verified layout data to manufacturing for mask making. The name comes from the days when data was delivered on magnetic tape.

SPICE.desc: A circuit simulator that calculates voltages and currents in transistor-level circuits in detail using device models. It is used for analog design and cell characterization.

高位合成(HLS).desc: Automatically generating RTL from an algorithm written in C, C++ or similar. It is used in developing FPGAs and accelerators.

クロックゲーティング.desc: A low-power design technique that stops the clock to idle circuit blocks, avoiding wasted switching power.

FPGA.desc: A chip whose logic configuration the user can rewrite after manufacture. It is used for prototypes, low-volume products and ASIC verification.

LVS.desc: Short for layout versus schematic: checking that the connectivity extracted from the layout matches the schematic or netlist. It is always run before tape-out, along with DRC.

ミニエンバイロメント.desc: Keeping only the small space around the wafers highly clean. Sealed carriers such as FOUPs combined with EFEMs on the tools lower the cleanliness required of the room as a whole, reducing cost.

OHT(天井走行式無人搬送車).desc: Vehicles that run along ceiling rails and automatically carry FOUPs between tools. They are the backbone of automated transport in 300 mm fabs.

FFU(ファンフィルタユニット).desc: A unit combining a fan with a high-efficiency filter. Arrays of them in the cleanroom ceiling blow clean air downward.

EFEM.desc: Short for equipment front end module: the unit at the front of a tool that opens FOUPs and transfers wafers into the tool in a clean environment. It includes load ports and a transfer robot.

HEPAフィルタ.desc: A high-efficiency air filter that captures at least 99.97% of 0.3 µm particles. Filters that capture even finer particles are ULPA filters.

局所排気装置.desc: Equipment that draws in gases and mists at their source, such as tools handling chemicals, and exhausts them. It keeps workers from inhaling hazardous substances.

爆発下限界(LEL).desc: The lowest concentration in air at which a flammable gas can burn or explode. Gas detectors are often set to alarm at a percentage of this level.

酸素欠乏(酸欠).desc: A condition in which the oxygen concentration in air falls below 18%. It tends to occur where large amounts of nitrogen are used or in confined spaces, and can cause unconsciousness within a few breaths.

リスクアセスメント.desc: Identifying the hazards of tasks or chemicals, estimating the size of the risks and deciding countermeasures in order of priority.

ロックアウト・タグアウト(LOTO).desc: A procedure that isolates energy sources such as power and gas before maintenance and fits locks and tags so no one can accidentally restore them during the work.

シリコンサイクル.desc: The recurring boom-and-bust pattern of the semiconductor market driven by supply and demand. One cause is that fabs take years to build, so supply lags changes in demand.

SoC(システムオンチップ).desc: An LSI that integrates the functions a system needs, such as CPU, GPU, memory controller and communications, on one chip. The heart of a smartphone is a typical example.

ASIC(特定用途向けIC).desc: An LSI designed specifically for one application or customer. It beats general-purpose chips on performance and power, but high development costs suit it to high-volume uses.

MPW(マルチプロジェクトウエハ).desc: Prototyping several customers' designs together on one wafer (one mask set). Sharing the expensive mask cost makes it popular with universities and startups.

デナードスケーリング.desc: The rule that shrinking transistor dimensions and supply voltage by the same factor gives faster, denser circuits at constant power density. It broke down in the mid-2000s when voltages could no longer be lowered easily.

ディスクリート半導体.desc: The category of semiconductor products that perform one function as a single device, such as diodes, individual transistors and power MOSFETs, as opposed to integrated circuits.

2.5D実装.desc: Placing several chips side by side on an intermediate substrate such as a silicon interposer and connecting them with dense, fine wiring. It is used, for example, to connect GPUs and HBM.

3D実装.desc: Stacking chips vertically and connecting them with TSVs or hybrid bonding. Shorter connections improve speed and power, but heat removal becomes a challenge.

再配線層(RDL).desc: A wiring layer formed on a chip or wafer surface to route pads out to the positions of the external terminals. It is used in fan-out packages and interposers.

マイクロバンプ.desc: A bump far smaller than an ordinary solder ball, used to connect TSV-stacked chips or chips to an interposer. The pitch is a few tens of micrometers.

UCIe.desc: Short for Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express: an industry-standard die-to-die interface intended to let chiplets from different companies connect to each other.

CoWoS.desc: TSMC's 2.5D packaging technology, which places logic chips and HBM side by side on a silicon interposer. It is widely used for AI GPUs and similar products.

FD-SOI(完全空乏型SOI).desc: Building transistors in a very thin silicon layer on buried oxide so the channel is fully depleted. The channel can be lightly doped, and body bias can tune the threshold voltage easily.

EOT(等価酸化膜厚).desc: The thickness of SiO2 that would give the same gate capacitance as a gate insulator such as a high-k film. A physically thick film can have a small EOT, giving high capacitance while limiting tunneling current.

ランダムドーパントゆらぎ(RDF).desc: Threshold-voltage variation in small transistors caused by statistical variation in the number and position of dopant atoms in the channel. FinFETs and FD-SOI, which allow lightly doped channels, reduce it.

SADP(自己整合ダブルパターニング).desc: Forming spacers on the sidewalls of a core pattern, removing the core and using the spacers as the mask to make a pitch half of what lithography alone allows. Doing it twice is SAQP.

ゲートラスト(リプレースメントメタルゲート).desc: Building the transistor first with a dummy gate, then removing it after high-temperature steps such as source/drain activation and replacing it with a high-k dielectric and metal gate.

DTCO(設計・技術協調最適化).desc: Optimizing cell area and performance by considering circuit design and process technology together, as scaling becomes harder.

ピエゾ抵抗効果.desc: The change in a material's electrical resistivity under mechanical stress. It is especially large in silicon and is used in semiconductor pressure sensors and similar devices.

ホール素子.desc: A sensor that detects magnetic fields using the Hall effect: a magnetic field applied to a current-carrying semiconductor produces a voltage perpendicular to both. It is used, for example, to sense motor rotation.

コリオリ力.desc: An apparent force acting perpendicular to the motion of an object moving in a rotating frame. Vibratory MEMS gyroscopes detect angular rate from the displacement it causes.

ボッシュプロセス(Deep RIE).desc: A dry-etching technique that alternates short etch and sidewall-passivation steps to cut deep, vertical holes and trenches in silicon. It is used for MEMS and TSVs.

スティクション.desc: The sticking of tiny moving MEMS parts to the substrate through surface tension or surface adhesion, so they no longer move. It often happens during drying after sacrificial-layer removal.

陽極接合.desc: Joining silicon to sodium-containing glass by heating them together while applying a voltage. It is used, for example, to seal MEMS devices.

シラン(SiH4).desc: A gas compound of silicon and hydrogen used as the source for CVD of polysilicon, silicon oxide and silicon nitride. It ignites spontaneously in air, so it is handled under strict control.

ホスフィン(PH3).desc: A gas compound of phosphorus and hydrogen used to introduce n-type dopant (phosphorus) into silicon. It is extremely toxic.

アルシン(AsH3).desc: A gas compound of arsenic and hydrogen used to introduce n-type dopant (arsenic) and to grow compound semiconductors such as GaAs. It is extremely toxic.

マスフローコントローラ(MFC).desc: A device in deposition and etch tools that precisely measures the mass flow of a gas and holds it at a set value.

SEM(走査電子顕微鏡).desc: A microscope that scans a finely focused electron beam over a sample and detects secondary electrons and other signals to image the surface. It resolves features of a few nanometers, far beyond optical microscopes.

AFM(原子間力顕微鏡).desc: A microscope that traces a sharp tip over a sample and measures fine surface topography from the forces between tip and surface. It is used, for example, to evaluate surface roughness.

EDX(エネルギー分散型X線分光).desc: An analysis method that measures the energies of characteristic X-rays emitted under an electron beam to identify which elements are present and how much. It is used with SEM or TEM.

XPS(X線光電子分光法).desc: An analysis method that determines the elements in the top few nanometers of a surface and their chemical bonding states from the energies of photoelectrons emitted under X-ray irradiation.

TXRF(全反射蛍光X線分析).desc: An analysis method that shines X-rays at a grazing angle so they totally reflect, then sensitively measures the fluorescent X-rays from trace metal contamination on the wafer surface.

FIB(集束イオンビーム).desc: An instrument that mills or deposits material with a finely focused ion beam. It is used for cross-sectioning tiny areas, preparing thin TEM samples and editing circuits.

XRD(X線回折).desc: An analysis method that shines X-rays on a crystal and uses the angles and intensities of the diffracted beams to determine crystal structure, lattice constant, film strain and crystal quality.

欠陥検査装置.desc: Equipment that finds particles and pattern defects on wafers, for example by detecting scattered light or by comparing images of neighboring dies.

時間的局所性.desc: The tendency to access the same data or instructions again soon after a first access, as with variables reused inside a loop. One of the reasons caches work.

空間的局所性.desc: The tendency to access addresses near one just accessed, as when reading an array in order. It is why caches fetch data a whole cache line at a time.

ダイレクトマップ方式.desc: A cache organization in which each address can be placed in exactly one location. It is simple with short hit time, but prone to conflict misses when addresses compete for the same slot.

セットアソシアティブ方式.desc: A cache organization in which data can go in any of several locations (ways) within the one set selected by the address. An n-way cache compares n tags in parallel on each access.

フルアソシアティブ方式.desc: A cache organization in which any data can be placed in any location. It has no conflict misses but must compare against every tag, so it suits small structures such as TLBs rather than large caches.

キャッシュライン.desc: The unit in which data moves between a cache and the level below, also called a cache block. Many CPUs use 64 bytes, and the low address bits give the position (offset) within the line.

ライトスルー方式.desc: A write policy that writes to the level below (such as main memory) at the same time as the cache. The lower level stays up to date, but write traffic is heavy, so it is paired with a write buffer.

ライトアロケート.desc: A policy that, on a write miss, first brings the line into the cache and then writes it. Usually paired with write-back; writing directly to the lower level without fetching is called no-write-allocate.

初期参照ミス.desc: A cache miss that inevitably occurs on the first access to data. A larger cache does not reduce it, but larger lines or prefetching can.

容量ミス.desc: A cache miss caused by the working set being larger than the cache. It occurs even in a fully associative cache and is reduced by a larger cache or by improving data reuse.

競合ミス.desc: A cache miss caused when several blocks compete for the same set and evict each other even though capacity remains. Higher associativity or shifting data placement reduces it.

LRU(Least Recently Used).desc: A cache replacement policy that evicts the least recently used data. It exploits temporal locality well, but exact tracking is costly with many ways, so approximations are used.

プリフェッチ.desc: Loading data into the cache before it is requested because it is likely to be needed soon. Hardware prefetchers detect access patterns, and software prefetching uses explicit instructions.

平均メモリアクセス時間(AMAT).desc: The average time per memory access, computed as hit time + miss rate × miss penalty. A basic metric for comparing cache designs.

ミスペナルティ.desc: The extra time needed to fetch data from the next level when a cache miss occurs, determined by the lower level's access time and the line transfer time.

ループブロッキング.desc: An optimization that processes large arrays in small blocks that fit in the cache so loaded data is reused many times before eviction. Very effective for matrix multiplication.

ノンブロッキングキャッシュ.desc: A cache that keeps servicing other accesses while a miss is outstanding. It can handle multiple misses at once, overlapping and hiding memory latency.

特権モード.desc: A CPU operating mode reserved for the OS kernel, in which dangerous operations such as setting page tables and controlling I/O are allowed. It is distinguished from user mode, where applications run.

システムコール.desc: The mechanism by which applications ask the OS for services such as file I/O or memory allocation. A dedicated instruction raises an exception that switches to privileged mode and invokes the kernel.

割り込みハンドラ.desc: The routine a CPU runs when an interrupt or exception occurs. It saves the interrupted state, handles the cause and returns. Handlers should be kept as short as possible.

割り込みベクタテーブル.desc: A table listing, for each type of interrupt or exception, the start address of its handler. The CPU indexes it by the cause number to find where to begin handling.

ページテーブル.desc: A table recording the mapping from virtual page numbers to physical page numbers. The OS builds one per process, and the CPU's MMU walks it to translate addresses. Each entry also holds protection bits.

ページフォルト.desc: An exception raised when an accessed page is not mapped to physical memory or the access type is not permitted. The OS either supplies the page and retries the instruction or treats it as an illegal access.

デマンドページング.desc: Loading a program's pages into physical memory only when first accessed and a page fault occurs, rather than all at once. It speeds startup and saves memory for unused parts.

コピーオンライト.desc: Sharing duplicated memory with the original at first and copying a page only when either side tries to write it. It speeds process creation and saves memory.

スラッシング.desc: A state in which physical memory is so short that pages are constantly evicted and reloaded, and little useful work gets done. It is relieved by running fewer processes or adding memory.

コンテキストスイッチ.desc: Switching the process or thread running on a CPU. Registers, the program counter and other state are saved and restored, and switching processes also switches address spaces.

ASID(アドレス空間識別子).desc: A number tagged onto each TLB entry indicating which process's address space the translation belongs to. The TLB need not be flushed on a process switch, reducing TLB misses afterward.

TLBシュートダウン.desc: On a multiprocessor, the procedure for making other cores discard stale translations from their TLBs after a page table is modified. It uses inter-processor interrupts or instructions that broadcast the invalidation to all cores, and is costly.

メモリマップドI/O.desc: Assigning peripheral registers to specific addresses in the same address space as memory and accessing them with ordinary load and store instructions. That region is configured as uncached.

デバイスドライバ.desc: An OS component that operates a specific peripheral. It handles the device's registers and interrupts and lets applications use the device through a common interface.

IOMMU.desc: A unit that translates and protects the addresses peripherals use for DMA. It keeps devices from writing to unauthorized memory and is also used when assigning devices to virtual machines.

ハイパーバイザ.desc: Software that runs multiple virtual machines on one computer, allocating CPU, memory and devices to each guest OS and isolating them from one another. Also called a virtual machine monitor.

入れ子ページング.desc: Hardware that walks two levels of page tables in succession, one managed by the guest OS and one by the hypervisor. It reduces hypervisor intervention and speeds up virtualization.

NMI(マスク不可能割り込み).desc: An interrupt that is always accepted regardless of interrupt masking. It is used to report uncorrectable memory errors, serious hardware faults and watchdog events.
